timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Hello children, welcome to EVS class.
I hope you all are doing well.
Today let's start with new topic.
Tell me children, have you all observed the sky?
What do you see in the sky?
Yes, absolutely right.
We can see the sun, the moon and the stars in the sky.
We can see the sun in daytime and the moon and the stars at night.
They are called heavenly bodies.
The sun, the moon and the stars are called the heavenly bodies.
And our today's topic is heavenly bodies.
Let's discuss this topic in the 10th.
Let's start.
The sun is a very large hot ball.
The sun is made of very hot gases.
It is far, far away from the earth.
The sun gives us heat and light.
The family of sun consists of sun and 8 planets.
All the 8 planets move around the sun.
The sun is in the center of the system.
This system is known as solar system.
The 8 planets that move around the sun are mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn,
Uranus, Neptune.
These planets follow a fixed path around the sun called orbit.
Mercury is the closest planet to the sun.
It is very hot and it is the smallest planet.
Jupiter is the biggest planet.
Venus is the brightest planet.
Earth is the third planet from the sun and it is a home planet.
Earth is the only planet that has life.
There is land and lots of water on Earth so it looks blue.
The moon is much nearer to the earth than the sun.
The moon is smaller than the sun.
We see different shapes of moon on different days.
At night we see thousands of twinkling stars in the sky.
Stars are far away so they appear very small.
Stars have their own life.
Now let's learn conversation sentences on heavenly bodies.
There are 8 planets in a solar system and one star that is called Sun.
These planets move around the sun in a path called orbit.
We get heat and light from Sun.
Jupiter is the biggest planet and Mercury is the smallest planet.
We leave on Earth which is the third planet from the sun.
Let's repeat the conversation sentences.
Heavenly bodies.
There are 8 planets in a solar system and one star that is called Sun.
These planets move around the sun in a path called orbit.
We get heat and light from Sun.
Jupiter is the biggest planet and Mercury is the smallest planet.
We leave on Earth which is the third planet from the sun.
So children, today we learnt about the heavenly bodies, Sun, Moon, Stars and the planets.
I hope you all have understood the topic very well and you all have enjoyed it.
Keep revising, bye, see you in the next class.
